value.desc: The read you turn outward runs inward too. It holds you to a standard that never quite says done.
You often know something before anyone is ready to hear it. The distance between those two moments is a lonely place, and it's hard to name.
People feel sized up around you even when you've said nothing. It isn't coldness, but it reads as coldness, and you're tired of explaining the difference.
You call things complete before they've fully arrived. The clarity that recognizes finished work can misread what's still becoming.
Your read circles without landing. You reach something true, find a reason to look again, and end up back where you started, still unsure it counts.
